properties.project_name: Boomitra Carbon Farming in the Indo-Gangetic Plains
properties.methodology: VM0042 Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Boomitra Carbon Farming in the Indo-Gangetic Plains
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: This project intends to help farmers adopt new improved agriculture practices in the Indo-Gangetic Plains of the Indian subcontinent. Improved agriculture practices include crop residue management, natural farming, crop rotations and more, which enable cropland soils to improve their carbon sequestration capabilities. The region contains large numbers of small and marginal farmers who are highly susceptible to reductions in yields arising from climate change, and there is a strong need for programs and interventions to help them adapt. In this context, improved agricultural practices provide the opportunity and the power to reverse land degradation and return carbon to the soil, creating carbon removals while improving overall soil health. In this project, farmers adopt a variety of improved agriculture practices. These practices are proven ways to increase soil organic carbon, and enable farmers to improve their productivity: increases in soil organic carbon improve the ability of soils to store moisture and nutrients, and thus also help to increase yields. Boomitra’s research has shown that farmers face various barriers in the adoption of these practices, and this project works towards helping farmers to surmount these barriers, while working with partners to create feasible and sustainable solutions that promote behavioral change at the grassroots level. The financial benefits from carbon credits will provide a direct boost to the livelihoods of these farmers, many of whom are small and marginal farmers.

properties.project_name: Grouped rooftop solar power project by SAEL Limited
properties.methodology: AMS-I.F. Renewable electricity generation for captive use and mini-grid
properties.verra_project_name_current: Grouped rooftop solar power project by SAEL Limited
properties.verra_project_description: The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops of educational institutions in various states of India by SAEL Limited (Previously, Sukhbir Agro Energy Ltd). All the rooftop solar panel units involved in the project are implemented under RESCO model where SAEL acts as a RESCO (Renewable Energy Service Company). Being the RESCO, SAEL has developed, installed, financed, operates and owns the rooftop solar power units and supplies power generated from the project to the consumers on whose premises the rooftop SPV panels are set up. The building owners are the customers of the power generated from the rooftop solar panels who purchase the power from SAEL Limited under long term power purchase agreements signed for 25 years. The purchased power by the customers is either consumed/utilized by the customers for in the buildings premises or injected to the grid of the Distribution Utility under the mechanism of net metering. Under the concept of Net Metering, the customers are charged only for the net power that they consume from the electricity service provider that has accumulated over a specific period. In other words, if their renewable energy generating systems make more electricity than consumed, they may be credited or paid for the excess electricity contributed to the grid over the same period. Net metering is also a way to increase the energy in the power grid to keep up with increase in demand during peak power use times, and this is of particular interest to states facing power shortages.

properties.project_name: Replacement of ICLs with LED lamps in Gujarat, India
properties.methodology: AMS-II.C. Demand-side energy efficiency activities for specific technologies
properties.verra_project_name_current: Replacement of ICLs with LED lamps in Gujarat, India
properties.verra_project_description: The purpose of this Grouped project “Replacement of ICLs with LED lamps in Gujarat, India” is to reduce fossil-fuel based electricity consumption in the Rural households of Gujarat by introducing more energy efficient LED lamps to replace incandescent lightbulbs (“ICLs”), This would result in reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. The overall penetration of LED in India is still at a nascent stage with rural India favoring conventional power guzzlers over CFLs and LED lightbulbs. Other barriers include reluctance to accept change, uncertainty about performance and lack of trust. The ordinary incandescent bulb is extremely energy inefficient for lighting when compared to LED. An ICL bulb requires 60 watts of power to emit around 700 lumens of light whereas LED bulb can emit 700 lumen by consuming just 9 watts. About 95% of the energy in LEDs is converted into light, and only 5% is wasted as heat. Despite being inefficient, ICLs are the most preferred option. The replacement of ICLs with energy efficient LED bulbs will reduce energy consumption, thus resulting in less GHG emissions. The Grouped project (GP) will be located within geographical boundary of Gujarat in India. The Project Instance (PI) 1 in this GP is estimated to generate a total of 537,990 tCO2e and an annual average of 53,799 tCO2e emission reductions over the crediting period of 10 years (15 April 2022 to 14 April 2032).

properties.project_name: INDIA CARBON PROGRAM:AWD/DSR
properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: INDIA CARBON PROGRAM:AWD/DSR
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: India is one of the world's largest producers of rice and exporter of rice in the world. Rice cultivation is the most important agricultural operation in India, not only in terms of food security but also in terms of livelihood and plays a major part in the economy. It is a known fact that rice fields emit methane into the environment that contributes to global warming. The project plans to promote improved water management practices in rice cultivation instead of using the traditional practice of continuously flooded irrigation. AWD/DSR are proven methods to reduce methane emission by as much as 48% compared to flooded conditions where large amounts of methane (CH4) gets generated because of anaerobic decomposition. This project is expected to generate important co-benefits of reducing water usage during rice cultivation, decrease pest and disease attacks, improve soil health etc. Further they are also beneficial for reduced cost of cultivation for small land holders. In the first instance, the project is planned to be implemented in 8,112 hectares in Punjab and Haryana States.  During the project implementation, relevant technical training and advisory was provided for the farmers to help them conduct AWD/DSR during rice cultivation. The total GHG emissions reductions due to the implementation of the project activity is estimated to be 380,225  tCO2e over 7 years.

properties.verra_project_name_current: Household Biogas Project in Uttarakhand, India
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources),Waste handling and disposal
properties.verra_project_description: The project activity involves operation of 13,549 household biogas plants (biodigesters) in Uttarakhand. Almost all Biodigesters are of 3m3 capacity. The plants covered under the project activity are commissioned from 22nd September 2020 onwards. The biogas plants are of deenbandhu model. The purpose of the project is to replace the commonly used inefficient wood fired mud stoves technology, with clean, sustainable, and efficient biogas. Each household utilizes cow dung to feed the digester to produce biogas for cooking purpose and heating water. properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: The proposed VCS ALM (Agricultural Land Management) project activity aims at developing a carbon sequestration project funded by Godrej Agrovet Ltd. (GAVL) in the watershed areas of Barwani district, Madhya Pradesh in collaboration with NABARD (National Bank for  Agriculture and Rural Development) Integrated Watershed Development Programme (IWDP). The project integrates adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM) practices in the context of watershed development (as per NABARD WDF Guidelines) activities. The project is implementing on the five village watersheds viz Mansoor, Mohaliya pani, Sidri, Sulgaon and Wajhar of the Niwali Block of the District, Barwani, which is the part of the major River Kajalmata and comes under the ‘Kajalmata Watershed Project’. The identified watershed villages are most suitable for the project activity (SALM Farming) intervention as it is reported with extensive agriculture activities, but with high levels of soil erosion & degradation and falls under the IX th Agro climatic regions i.e. Western Plateau and Hills. The project activity achieves Godrej’s (Godrej Agrovet Ltd. GAVL), sustainability goal of ‘Good & Green by 2025’ which ensures the carbon neutrality and water positivity as the target’s needs. The project is implementing through in active participation with the NGO AKRSP(I) (AGA KHAN RURAL SUPPORT PROGRAMME (INDIA)), the concerned Project  Implementing Agency (PIA) for the SALM project implementation in the watershed areas. The estimate of annual average GHG reductions and removals through adoption of SALM practices in the agricultural landscape is 23154 tCO2e and for the first renewal crediting period of 20 years the total reductions estimations are 463074 tCO2e. The Project activities are carried out and monitored according to approved VCS methodology VM0017: Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management.

properties.project_name: Core Carbon Sustainable Rice Productions
properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Core Carbon Sustainable Rice Productions
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Paddy fields are the most dominant anthropogenic sources of methane to the atmosphere (5-20% of the total emission from all anthropogenic sources ). Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes to the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The annual amount of CH4 emitted from a given area of rice is a function of the number and duration of crops grown, water regimes before and during the cultivation period, and organic and inorganic soil amendments. Soil type, temperature, and rice cultivar also affect CH4 emissions. This CH4 emission-intensive cultivation method will be targeted by the proposed programme, that will involve the implementation of the technology/measures that result in reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice cropping soils and thus reduced generation of methane. The project activity comprises of grouped projects of rice fields implementing the following methods: (a) Rice farms that change the water regime during the cultivation period from continuously to intermittent flooded conditions and/or a shortened period of flooded conditions; (b) Alternate wetting and drying method (AWD) (c) Rice farms that change their rice cultivation practice from transplanted to direct-seeded rice (DSR). Thus, the measure will consist of AWD and/or DSR in combination with adjusted water management system in rice cultivation.

The project activity is developed by Core CarbonX Solutions Private Limited and is targeted to be implemented in rural areas located in all the districts in the states of India. This project seeks to increase access of households and communities to improved cookstoves by disseminating high thermal efficiency and low greenhouse gas emitting cooking stoves. This will in turn reduce deforestation as less firewood would be utilised for cooking. It will also avoid soil erosion and nutrient loss from degradation of forests. The improved cook stoves to be distributed would provide co-benefits to users in the form of reduced exposure to health-damaging indoor air pollutions due to the burning of firewood in traditional inefficient cook stoves, and create decent work for local people leading to a sustainable source of income. Gathering of firewood and cooking are major tasks undertaken primarily by women and young girls especially in rural communities. The time saved from gathering firewood and cooking can be spent on productive, educational and income earning activities. The location of the project The project location is in the state of Odisha and Jharkhand in India initially and will expand to other states of India. properties.project_name: Waste Management Project-1 by BoxLNG
properties.methodology: AMS-I.F. Renewable electricity generation for captive use and mini-grid; AMS-III.D. Methane recovery in animal manure management systems; AMS-III.AO. Methane recovery through controlled anaerobic digestion; VM0042 Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use; Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources); Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management; Transport; Waste handling and disposal
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use,Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources),Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management,Transport,Waste handling and disposal
properties.verra_project_name_current: Waste Management Project-1 by BoxLNG
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use,Energy industries (renewable/non-renewable sources),Livestock, enteric fermentation, and manure management,Transport,Waste handling and disposal
properties.verra_project_description: The project activity is an organic waste anaerobic digestion bio-refinery; the purpose of the project activity to recover and treat various types of organic wastes (including livestock manure) to convert them into biogas under an anaerobic process and then to produce Compressed Biogas (CBG) via “Bio-methanation process for further application in transportation sector. The total capacity of the bio-refinery has been proposed to be 250 Tons of waste per day; the proposed waste types under the project shall primarily include animal manures, agri-wastes and a nominal quantity of other mix wastes as well. The wastes to be considered under the project activity would have been otherwise openly decayed, leading to a significant quantity of methane emission in absence of the project activity. Additionally, the project proposes to have an off-grid solar unit within the project boundary to meet the captive power requirements of the plant leading to reduction of GHG emissions against grid power at baseline. Further, the by-products of the refinery shall be used for soil application to replace nitrogen based fertilizers which further reduces GHG emissions. Thus, the project aims to combine multiple baseline to achieve a high level of GHG emissions and thereby leading to sustainability. Due to high level of environmental and social involvement the project activity shall cater to various positive impacts which are related to more than 5 SDG indicators. The project is currently at pre-commissioning stage, expected to achieve commissioning during the last quarter of this year.

properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use

properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Under the Uttarakhand Forest Resource Management Project (UFRMP), Uttarakhand Forest Department (UKFD) has tackled forest degradation in over 800 Van Panchayats across the state. VPs were treated in Ranikhet Soil Conservation Forest Division. Out of these Van Panchayats, 18 Van Panchayats have been selected for developing carbon finance project. Anthropogenic pressures such as unsustainable extraction of fuel wood, overgrazing of cattle,anthropogenic forest fire, and unsustainable extraction of Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs) are responsible for forest degradation and deforestation in these Van Panchayats. Various eco-restoration activities are implemented by UFRMP with an objective to enhance restoration of the degraded forests by empowering village community. These activities include assisted natural regeneration, protection through fencing, soil and water conservation, alternative livelihood development including other better forest management practices like fire management and forest patrolling.

properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: METHANE EMISSION REDUCTION PROJECT THROUGH INTERMITTENT FLOODING IN RICE CULTIVATION
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Methane emissions through flooded rice cultivation is one of the largest sources of methane into the atmosphere. Approximately 15-20% of annual total methane emissions come from the paddy fields. Methane is a potent gas with a Global Warming Potential (GWP) of 28 is significant gas in the context of climate change. Therefore, it is essential to address the methane emissions from the rice farming to mitigate climate change.  The proposed project activity aims at the reducing methane emissions from the paddy cultivation. The project has introduced direct seeded rice (DSR) technique to irrigated rice cultivation. Prior to the project activity, rice was cultivated in conventional manner with flooding of paddy farms for at least 100 days.

properties.project_name: Developing voluntary carbon market project for Periyar Tiger Reserve in India
properties.methodology: VM0037 Methodology for Implementation of REDD+ Activities in Landscapes Affected by Mosaic Deforestation and Degradation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Developing voluntary carbon market project for Periyar Tiger Reserve in India
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Tiger Reserves are the storehouse of ecosystem services and a majority of rural population depend on forest resources for their day-to-day livelihood. This dependence is in the form of collection of a variety of Non-Timber Forest Produce (NTFP) and collection of firewood and fodder for subsistence and livelihood purposes. Due to this dependence on forest resources and lack of sufficient infrastructure, the local communities venture in the forest areas resulting in degradation of pristine forest and causing human wildlife conflicts. This results in loss of human lives, and wild animals in a retaliatory process. Hence, there is a need to develop a dedicated finance mechanism which shall help in mitigating the conflicts in an efficient way and lead to coexistence and harmony amongst forest fringe communities and wildlife. This project will result in enhancing carbon sequestration by reducing pressures on forests from unsustainable collection of firewood through sustainable firewood management and exploring energy efficient technologies and alternative fuel in and around Periyar Tiger Reserve, Kerala.

properties.verra_project_description: The objective of the project is to restore degraded mangrove ecosystems in the estuarine islands of several rivers in coastal Karnataka, including the Aghanashini, Sharavathi and Kali rivers, and their tributaries. The three rivers form an integral part of the coastal ecosystem of Uttara Kannada District of Karnataka, India.The project objective is to restore the degarded mangrove habitats through plantation of several, diverse native mangrove and mangrove associated species, including several species which had disappeared from the region following degradation and deforestation of the mangrove habitat.

properties.project_name: Providing Low Carbon Irrigation Access To Indian Farmers
properties.methodology: AMS-II.F. Energy efficiency and fuel switching measures for agricultural facilities and activities
properties.verra_project_name_current: Providing Low Carbon Irrigation Access To Indian Farmers
properties.verra_project_description: The proposed grouped project activity seeks to reduce greenhouse gases emissions by disseminating the high energy efficient solar water pumps for agricultural activities to Indian farmers who were using the inefficient electricity pumps in baseline scenario. The proposed grouped project activity seeks to increase access of solar water pumps which are zero greenhouse gas emitting being operated on the solar energy. Their old low efficiency and high greenhouse gas emitting electricity pumps would be replaced. The implementation of the project activity, will result in the reduction of consumption of grid electricity and DG sets & consequent emissions from combustion leading to climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objectives are reduction of greenhouse gases by promoting the renewable solar pumps to the farmers.

properties.verra_project_description: Enhance livelihood of rural and tribal communities in the project area by providing underserved, at-risk communities with improved cook stoves, employment opportunities, and by increasing awareness on both GHG emissions. Through this community-engaging project, we plan to introduce and teach clean cooking practices, reduce Household Air Pollution (HAP), and thereby lower health risks amongst rural and tribal households. The proposed project replaces traditional, high GHG emitting and low efficient stoves used in rural parts of the project area with Improved Cookstoves (ICS), which have more thermal efficiency and cause lesser air pollution. properties.verra_project_name_current: CORE CARBON VANAM IN JHARKHAND STATE 2
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: The proposed ARR VCS project plans to promote sustainable agroforestry for small-scale farmers to provide them with financial benefits and ensure GHG mitigation in the state of Jharkhand, India. The project is being conducted in the spread across all the districts of Jharkhand. CCX entered into carbon offset agreements with individual farmers of various districts of Jharkhand state for the provision of carbon credit advisory services to them. The individual farmers are the owners of the lands on which trees are being grown to sequester carbon and reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the atmosphere. CCX has mobilized the farmers in the selected states of India to plant various tree species on their lands. These tree species range from fruit-bearing trees like Indian blackberry, Guava, and Mango to commercial species like Teak, Mahogany Sandal, etc. The selected farmers have employed simple tree cultivation techniques involving planting saplings in the pits with minimum disturbance to the lands.

properties.verra_project_description: The “Decentralized Municipal Solid Waste to Compost Formation Project” (hereinafter referred to as the “proposed project activity”) is the implementation of a new composting plant with the purpose to avoid methane emissions from anaerobic decomposition of MSW in a landfill site through controlled aerobic decomposition in a composting process. properties.project_name: CORE CARBON VANAM(SERICULTURE) IN ODISHA STATE
properties.methodology: AR-ACM0003 Afforestation and reforestation of lands except wetlands
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: CORE CARBON VANAM(SERICULTURE) IN ODISHA STATE
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Core CarbonX Solutions Private Limited (CCX) is a carbon management consultancy company with registered office in the state of Odisha. CCX is the Project Proponent (PP) of the carbon offset project called “Core Carbon Vanam (Sericulture) in Odsha State”. CCX entered into carbon offset agreements with individual farmers of various districts of Odisha state for provision of carbon credit advisory services to them. The individual farmers are the owners of the lands on which trees are being grown to sequester carbon and reduce greenhouse gas emissions from the atmosphere. CCX has mobilized the farmers in the selected states of India to plant various tree species on their lands. These tree species range from trees like Asana, Arjuna covering Sericulture sector. Simple tree cultivation techniques involving planting saplings in the pits with minimum disturbance to the lands have been employed by the selected farmers. The villages under the project area predominantly have an agrarian economy where most of its population depends on agriculture. The major agroforestry plantation in these project districts (Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj & Sundergarh) are Asana, Arjuna etc . The planation was done by the farmers and utilized the subsidies to avail the saplings. The saplings do the sequestration of carbon dioxide at faster pace and ultimately reduces GHG emissions. The Project Activity will lead to considerable carbon sequestration in the project areas and will contribute strongly to the sustainable development of rural villages involved in the project. Initially, 6,300 hectares of land has been selected for the first project activity instance. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions or removals of 62811 tCO2e.

properties.project_name: EVI SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE PROGRAM
properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: EVI SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE PROGRAM
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: The purpose of this grouped project (Program) is to replace the traditional practice of flooded irrigation (baseline) with System of Root Intensification (SRI) technique in rice cultivation (project). SRI is an intermittent wet and dry technique of cultivation which induces positive socio-economic and environmental impacts by reducing water consumption and increasing crop yield compared to baseline. This also results in reduced GHG emission emissions associated with energy use in water pumping and methane avoidance associated with standing water in farm fields compared to the baseline. Increase in yield and reduced water and energy consumption also yields socio-economic benefits to the farmers. The first project activity instance (VPA) under the program is located in the state of Odisha in India. In the baseline, farmers were using traditional agriculture practice of rice cultivation and replaced it with SRI in the project activity. The area covered in this VPA is up to 500 hectares. In the project activity, emission reductions happen due to methane avoidance from the farm fields and reduced electricity consumption. However, emission reductions due to methane avoidance alone, are being claimed under the program. It is estimated that 60,000 tCO2e of emission reductions will be generated per annum.

properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Core CarbonX Solutions Private Limited (CCX) is a carbon management consultancy company with registered office in the state of Telangana. CCX is the Project Proponent (PP) of the carbon offset project called “Carbon Sequestration through Agroforestry by farmers in Telangana State”. CCX entered into carbon offset agreements with individual farmers of various districts of Telangana state for provision of carbon credit advisory services to them the districts covered under this project activity are Bhadradri Kothagudem, Hanamkonda, Jagithyal Jayashankar Bhupalapally, Kamareddy, Karimnagar, Khammam, Mahabubabad Mulugu & Warangal, Nagarkurnool, Nalgonda, Peddapelli and Suryapet. The villages under the project area predominantly have an agrarian economy where most of its population depends on agriculture. The project quantifies the GHG removals occurring from agroforestry plantations through the use of AR-ACM0003: “Afforestation and reforestation project activities implemented on lands other than wetlands”, Version 02.0 developed under the Clean Development Mechanism for large-scale plantations. The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. Such planting activity would result in carbon credits that would be sold in the carbon market to generate revenue.The project activity was implemented in 3029.69 hctres. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions or removals of 73,711 tCO2e.

properties.verra_project_description: The project involves installation of Solar Photovoltaic (SPV) Panels on rooftops and ground mounted in the premises of Hyderabad Metro Project by AMPSolar Generation Private Limited .All the rooftop and ground mounted solar panel units involved in the proj ect are implemented under DBFOT model , i.e., Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer. The owners of the metro project are the customers of the power generated from the rooftop and ground mounted solarpanels who purchase the power from AMPSolar Generation Private Limited under long term power purchase agreements . The purchased power by the customers is used for captive purpose and consumed/utilized by the customers in the metro stations and depots Before installation of the rooftop solar units, the Hyderabad Metro premises used to meet the electricity demand from the national grid of the India. The project thus replaces fossil fuel dominated grid electricity thereby reducing the equivalent amount of GHG emission.

properties.project_name: Core Carbon Sahaja Vyavasayam in Andhra Pradesh
properties.methodology: VM0017 Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Core Carbon Sahaja Vyavasayam in Andhra Pradesh
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Andhra Pradesh has been historically called the Rice Bowl of India and continues to be the country's largest rice producer. The agriculture system forms the backbone of economic development and contributes 32.79 % of the total State Domestic Product. The proposed Natural Farming in Andhra Pradesh activity is practised by individual farmers practised by about 5,00,000 farmers and organic grower cooperatives covering 6,41,230 hectares of cropland in the state of Andhra Pradesh to be implemented in the first phase. The project aims at increasing the capacity of soil to sequester carbon, enhance the carbon sequestration by agroforestry practices such as planting of trees, reduce emissions from the use of synthetic fertilizers and reduce emissions from burning of crop residue by application of VCS methodology: VM0017 Sustainable Agricultural Land Management (SALM). Several SALM practices and technologies have been proven to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and prevent climate change by enhancing carbon storage in soils, preserving existing soil carbon, and reducing carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide emissions. Those practices include conservation tillage, cover crops, enhanced crop rotations, residue retention, agroforestry and avoidance of crop residue burning. The project holistically aims at achieving sustainable management practices which improve soil health, reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and develop the socio-economic status of the project area. The project aims to reduce and sequester carbon leading to estimated GHG emission reductions or removals (tCO2e) of 4830706 tCO2e / year. This project's climate benefits include emissions reduction or removals of approximately 193228248 tCO2e over the lifetime of the project.

properties.project_name: Community Based Forest Plantation in India

properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Community Based Forest Plantation in India
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: “Community Forest Plantation in India” is a combined Afforestation and sustainable development project carried out by farmers with the help of a project implementer. The associated project implementer is helping farmers to plant trees on the land which is identified as unproductive, and the area is highly water scarce. Farmers retain ownership of the trees, products, and land as well. Farmers received training from the project implementer for plantation and the project implementer (Greenovation) is providing plantation material (saplings, manure) to the farmers and further assistance in maintaining the required survival rate of the plantation. Carbon credits generated from this project will help in maintaining the survival rate of planted trees and support farmers. The total area expected to be covered in the project is around 10,000 hectares. The current plantations have been covered to plant 4,400 hectares in the country.The project participants are using the afforestation approach and planted thousands of trees on the land across the project boundary. In case of the absence of this project activity land would be continued to be less productive land or degraded land. The project will help in mitigating climate change for the next 40 years by sequestrating/removing the carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and creating a carbon pool. The project activity will result in an annual average of 1,40,882 tons of GHG removal and total removal of 56,35,266 tons of CO2 over the 40 years of the period.

properties.verra_project_name_current: Community Forestry Initiatives in India
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: “Community Forest Initiative in India” is an sustainable afforestation development project carried out by the local farmers with the help of a local NGO. The farmers plant trees on the abandoned wasteland allotted to the communities and retain ownership of the trees, produce, from forestation. Project activity has been planned for helping farmers in developing forest for which they have received plantation material, Irrigation technology and other training received from NGO to establish and maintain the planted forest. NGO empowers the large group of poor communities in West Bengal and Odisha states of India to create & manage the forest on degraded abandoned land to increase forest cover by planting fruit-bearing species. Apart from above, the NGOs helps in managing and sustainably harvesting the NTFPs (Non-Timber Forest Products) for participating farmers. The carbon credits from this project activity will also create a new ‘virtual’ cash crop for the participants, who gain all the direct benefits of growing trees and receive benefits based on the GHG benefits created by their efforts (as a result-based payment approach). The maturing trees and conservation activity will provide additional sustainable benefits such as income in form of the carbon payments, climate change mitigation self-resilience and sustainable. . The project will help in mitigating climate change for the next 40 years by sequestrating the carbon from the atmosphere and creating a natural biomass carbon pool. NGO has estimated that this project will result in an annual average of GHG removal of 1,45,278 tonnes/annual and total removals of 58,11,102 tonnes of CO2 for 40 years of project duration.

properties.verra_project_description: This project aims for the sustainable implementation and management of Afforestation activity that involves carbon sequestration on degraded lands through agroforestry plantation activities with species plantations in the multiple districts of India. The project includes multiple land parcels (continue and scattered). The project has been undertaken to plant agroforestry species on the land which was severly degraded in the baseline and continues to be degraded. Before the project activity, the project area was facing threat due to severe soil erosion from slash and burn rotations. The project tends to combat land degradation and emphasize the role of project in the UN sustainable development and land restoration agenda. The project activity is expected to reduce atmospheric CO2 by sequestration and storing in the form of biomass. The project is expected to be functional and remove CO2 from the atmosphere for 80 years of its lifetime with 30 years of renewable period. The Project activities are carried out and monitored according to the approved project methodology AR-ACM0003 for the first crediting period of 30 years. The project aims to remove an estimated 39,445 tCO2e annually and 11,83,343 tCO2e during the first crediting period.

properties.verra_project_description: The villages under the project area predominantly have an agrarian economy where most of its population depends on agriculture. The major agroforestry plantation in these project districts (Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj & Sundergarh) are Asana, Arjuna, Cashew and Mango. The plantation was done by the farmers and utilized subsidies to avail the saplings. The saplings do sequestration of carbon dioxide at a faster pace and ultimately reduce GHG emissions.  Initially, 10,520 hectares of land have been selected for the first project activity instance. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions or removals of 104,844 tCO2e. CCX company held workshops in the villages and advised the villagers to grow Asana & Arjuna, Cashew and Mango trees in a sustainable manner to earn carbon revenue. The idea of earning additional revenue caught the farmer’s attention, and they decided to enter into carbon-offset agreements with the CCX company.

properties.project_name: Ban Odisha 01
properties.methodology: AR-ACM0003 Afforestation and reforestation of lands except wetlands
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Ban Odisha 01
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Core CarbonX Solutions Private Limited (CCX) is a carbon management consultancy company with registered office in the state of Telangana. CCX is the Project Proponent (PP) of the carbon offset project called “Ban Odisha01” in all districts of Odisha. The Project Activity will lead to considerable carbon sequestration in the project areas and will contribute strongly to the sustainable development of rural villages involved in the project. The project quantifies the GHG removals occurring from agroforestry plantations through the use of AR-ACM0003: “Afforestation and reforestation project activities implemented on lands other than wetlands”, Version 02.0 developed under the Clean Development Mechanism for large-scale plantations. The project plans to generate carbon credits for the voluntary market under the VCS standard. Such planting activity would result in carbon credits that would be sold in the carbon market to generate revenue. As per the Carbon-offset agreement entered into between the farmers and CCX, 60%-80 of the carbon income generated from the sale of carbon credits would be distributed among the farmers. The project activity was implemented in 1900 hectares. Through carbon sequestration by the planted trees, the project is expected to generate annual average GHG emission reductions or removals of 15671 tCO2e.

properties.project_name: Optimization of the Nitrogen fertilizer in India and Thailand by using satellite images analysis
properties.methodology: VM0042 Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use

properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Sagri Co., Ltd is going to decrease the usage of Nitrogen Fertilizer in India and Thailand by using the soil detect technology by satellite images. Indian farmers are over-applying chemical fertilizers. However, the rising price of chemical fertilizers has put small-scale farmers' farming operations in a critical situation. In addition, excessive application of nitrogen fertilizers is bad for the environment for the following reasons. First, excessive nitrogen fertilizer applied to the ground causes excessive denitrification. In the process of denitrification, N₂O, a greenhouse gas with a greenhouse effect about 300 times greater than CO₂, is emitted. In addition, excessive application of synthetic nitrogen fertilizers can cause water pollution. Excess nitrogen that runs off into rivers and streams and enters people's bodies through drinking water and aquatic products poses a health hazard. Therefore, by applying the appropriate amount of nitrogen fertilizer to the soil, the amount of nitrogen fertilizer applied can be reduced, helping farmers to operate their farms, preventing global warming, and reducing health hazards to people. Sagri is engaged in the business of solving global issues related to agriculture and the environment by combining satellite data and AI machine learning technology, and is promoting its core technology, AI Polygon, which uses image technology with AI to analyze high-resolution satellite data and automatically plot farmland in Japan and overseas. Sagri is also developing a technology to analyze soil chemical indices on farmland after plowing, using wavelength data obtained from satellite data and AI-based machine learning.In this project, Sagri will use this technology to analyze soil chemical indices to determine the appropriate amount of fertilizer to be applied, and will receive carbon credits for encouraging farmers to use variable fertilizer application.

properties.project_name: GHG EMISSION REDUCTION THROUGH INTERMITTENT FLOODING IN RICE FIELDS
properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation; VM0042 Methodology for Improved Agricultural Land Management
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use

properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: The project activity is an 'Alternate wetting and drying (AWD)' activity that is a water saving strategy in irrigated rice production. The main objective of the project is to switch from continuously flooded rice fields to fields that alternately encompass flooded and non-flooded phases which can save significant amount of irrigation water. Thus, the project activity has been designed to change from continuously flooded to intermittent flooded condition during rice cultivation which is conducted in different blocks in the district of Bhopal, Hoshangabad, Raisen and Sehore of the state of Madhya Pradesh, in India. A total of 8,085 hectare for single-cropping rice has been covered under the project activity. During rice cultivation, controllable irrigation and drainage according to rice growth requirements can save water resources, and also at the same time will also reduce methane emission from soil organic matter under anaerobic conditions (in the flooded state). Additionally, in the project activity compost will be used for soil application in the rice fields and thus replace the application of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer. It is estimated that about 58,722 tCO2e emission reductions will be generated annually across the crediting period.

properties.methodology: VMR0006 Energy Efficiency and Fuel Switch Measures in Thermal Applications
properties.verra_project_name_current: Improved Cookstove Distribution by Climate Detox Private Limited- Phase I
properties.verra_project_description: The objective of the project is to provide a fuel-efficient cookstove termed as Improved Cook Stove (ICS) to the rural parts in the state of Gujarat in India. The use of Improved Cook Stove for daily cooking activity will reduce the greenhouse gas emissions. The project will replace the traditional cook stove primarily used in the rural households which consumes huge quantity of wood in cooking. The ICS is manufactured in such a way that it has significantly high thermal efficiency which will lead to the low fuel wood consumption and thus less greenhouse gas emissions would occur. The project activity will also positively impact the health and daily lifestyle of the rural people. ICS is proven to produce less smoke and thus it will reduce the respiratory heath issues which happens in the traditional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS beneficiaries will have to spend less time to collect the firewood and this saved time they will use in taking care of their family, kids and other productive work. The cookstove is also a safer equipment as it is closed from all sides hence users and their family will be in a safer environment. Climate Detox Pvt Ltd and Siddhant Energy Consultants are the project participants for this project. The distribution of ICS will be done in the rural areas under the supervision of an equipped team. All the ICS will be supplied by an experience manufacturer. ICS has been tested in the reputed laboratory for thermal efficiency. In the absence of project activities, the baseline scenario is that the target population continues to consume non-renewable wood fuel to meet similar thermal energy needs as provided by project cookstoves. Under this project activity, project participant has planned to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in the rural area of India. The estimated annual average greenhouse gas removal from the project is 368,478 tCO2e.

properties.verra_project_description: The proposed project activity under VCS will mobilize resource-poor farmers to raise tree plantations on vacant farmlands. It proposes to link resource poor farmers and end users of wood products in order to optimize the land use and to facilitate the co-ordination of wood producers, agronomists, industry, social enterprises and non-governmental organizations to improve the livelihood opportunities of rural households. The project activity is implemented on the degraded farmlands or lands used for rainfed subsistence agriculture. Various environment friendly technology-based agroforestry practices and Natural Climate Solutions (NCS) will be adopted to help climate change adaptation and mitigation as part of sustainable land management. This project will optimise the land use and generate Emission Reductions (ERs). The amount of carbon sequestered through the project activity will be measured, quantified with reference to a baseline to determine the Emission Reductions (ERs) generated. The ERs will be calculated through Above Ground Biomass, Below Ground Biomass and Soil Organic Carbon. In the absence of the project, the lands would have remained degraded and the resource poor farmers would have continued to practice subsistence agriculture. The participation of small and marginal farmers as part of the VCS project makes this initiative unique in contributing to their land use choice, improvement of livelihood opportunities and in promoting their capacity to organize and implement climate change mitigation initiatives. The project implements reforestation on 13,500 ha of degraded private lands in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Orissa. The reforestation activities under the project were initiated in 2019. The project is estimated to generate 94,200 credits / year on average over a period of 20 years.

properties.project_name: DEVELOPING VOLUNTARY CARBON MARKET  PROJECT FOR FARMERS ADOPTNG  ALTERNATE WETTING AND DRYING (AWD)  METHOD FOR RICE CULTIVATION
properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: DEVELOPING VOLUNTARY CARBON MARKET  PROJECT FOR FARMERS ADOPTNG  ALTERNATE WETTING AND DRYING (AWD)  METHOD FOR RICE CULTIVATION
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Flooding conditions in rice fields emit the most CH4, while intermittently flooded rice fields create a high quantity of N2O. Emissions of GHGs from rice fields can be reduced by modifying irrigation patterns, regulating organic additives, and using suitable rate and quantity of Nitrogen fertilizer. Irrigation practice such as Alternate wetting and drying (AWD) method has been observed to reduce GHG emissions in comparison to the traditional method of flooding. The time intervals between dry and wet conditions help in the transition from aerobic to anaerobic soil conditions, thus alternate wetting, and drying method leads in a significant reduction in methane generation1. Thus, the project employs AWD method to reduce the CH4 emissions. This will also lead to reduction in the water consumption, thus decreasing the input cost of the farmer. Before implementation of the project activity, the farmers were following the traditional flooding method, leading to the emissions of methane in the atmosphere. The project proponent conducted training programs and meeting with the farmers to make them aware about the benefits of adopting AWD, followed by the distribution and installation of AWD pipe in the fields of enrolled farmers. The first instance of the project is located in Haryana state covering an area of 4973 hectares. Furthermore, as it is a grouped project, the project activity will be implemented in other rice growing states of India in the future instances. Annual average emissions from the project are 48,853 tCO2eq.

properties.verra_project_description: The proposed grouped project activity seeks to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by disseminating fuel-efficient cookstoves in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand & Bihar states of India. Biomass has been considered as one of the primeval resources of energy and it is among the most favoured matter utilized by mankind since thousands of years. Fuel wood is one of the commonly used sources of domestic energy in the rural areas of many developing nations. In rural areas of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Bihar, the primary source of fuel wood is dry and diseased trees, fallen wood scraps or branches. Various studies show that more than 70% of the rural population in the states targeted is dependent on fuel wood for cooking and other domestic purposes, which impacts the limited forest resources .The increase in demand for fuel wood degrades the biodiversity. The studies reveal that felling of trees for fuelwood is far greater than the rate of vegetational growth. ‘SDG13 Ventures Pte Ltd’ (herein after called as “SDG”) is project proponent along with ‘Offsetfarm Pte Ltd’ for this project. SDG through its representative in Host Country will coordinate with the users of ICS directly or through local partners or its representative to ensure that all requirements with respect to project activity, such as assisting with validation and registration, record keeping, monitoring and survey of households at a regular interval are met.

properties.methodology: VMR0006 Energy Efficiency and Fuel Switch Measures in Thermal Applications
properties.verra_project_name_current: Improved Cookstove Distribution by Climate Detox Private Limited - Phase III
properties.verra_project_description: The project's goal is to supply improved cook stove (ICS) in the rural areas of the Indian state of Rajasthan. ICS is an innovative cookstove that uses less fuel. The emissions of greenhouse gases will be decreased if improved cook stoves are used for daily cooking. The initiative will replace the conventional cook stove, which is mostly utilized in rural communities and uses a significant amount of wood to prepare food. The ICS is built with a remarkably high thermal efficiency, which will result in a minimal need for fuel wood use and less greenhouse gas emissions. The project activity will have a good effect on the rural residents' daily lives and health. It has been demonstrated that ICS produces less smoke, which will lessen the respiratory health problems that result from using a conventional cookstove. On the other hand, ICS recipients will spend less time gathering firewood, and they will use that time to care for their families, children, and other productive tasks. Additionally, because the cookstove is completely enclosed, users and their families will be in a safer environment. The baseline scenario assumes that in the absence of project activities, the target population will continue to use non-renewable wood fuel to satisfy thermal energy needs comparable to those met by project cookstoves. The project participant intends to distribute 50,000 Improved Cook Stoves in India's rural areas as part of this project activity. The project will remove 368,478 tCO2e of greenhouse gases on average each year. The project participants for this project are Climate Detox Pvt Ltd. And Siddhant Energy Consultants. Under the direction of a prepared team, ICS will be distributed in rural areas.

properties.verra_project_description: The purpose of the project is to replace the commonly used inefficient wood fired mud stoves technology, with clean, sustainable, and efficient biogas. Each household utilizes cattle dung to feed the digester to produce biogas for cooking purpose. This leads to reduction of greenhouse gas emissions by displacing conventionally used non-renewable biomass with renewable biogas and reduction of greenhouse gas emissions related to animal manure which is left to decay anaerobically. In addition, the hygienic conditions in the rural areas will be improved by an appropriate disposal of waste. Further, residue from the bio digesters can be used as organic fertilizer for land application. Project activity will contribute towards sustainable development by replacing non-renewable source of energy with biogas generated from the biodigesters. The Project is operational in India in the rural areas of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

properties.methodology: VM0047 Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Creation of Biodiverse Forests for Land Restoration and Community Development
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: The project activity “Creation of Biodiverse Forests for Land Restoration and Community Development” (referred as “the project”) is located in 5 districts in the Maharashtra state of India. The project works with individual farmers and community members across 5 districts of Maharashtra to help them afforest or reforest land that is fallow, unused or deforested thus helping to bring back lost biodiversity and creating green employment and income opportunities for community members. Forest plantations on unused or abandoned agricultural land are not only a great mitigation strategy, but also a great adaptation strategy. Biodiverse forests, as compared to traditional agriculture, are extremely resilient to extreme weather events like cyclones, drought, hailstorms and pest attacks. They thus can help provide a reliable source of supplemental income to the agrarian and tribal communities in India that are facing declining yields and income loss due to climate-change induced erratic rainfall and extreme weather events. The project involves planting of over over 120 different species of trees, shrubs, grasses and creepers to create small carbon-sequestering pockets of land with about 1000 trees / hectare that can provide a source of fruit, leaf, bark and oilseed harvest for community members, while also bringing back lost soil carbon onto the land and attracting a wide variety of pollinators like birds and bees to the area. Along the boundary of the tree plantation two to three different species of bamboo will be planted that community members can harvest in a sustainable manner for timber. properties.verra_project_description: Rice is the country's most significant agricultural product; it is grown on 43.86 million hectares in India and contributes to more than 20% of world rice output (158.2 Tg in 2013). Rice is farmed in practically every state in India, and its production is directly related to the country's food security. Additionally, it is a significant source of income and employment. Rice production, on the other hand, is a substantial source of critical and long-lasting GHGs such as CH 4 and N 2 O, posing a huge threat to sustainable agriculture. Rice fields provide approximately 30% and 11% of total agricultural CH 4 and N 2 O emissions, respectively. According to early US-EPA study, paddy in India produced around 37.8 Tg CH 4 per year. GHG emissions from rice fields may be minimized by changing irrigation patterns, managing organic additions, and utilizing the appropriate rate and amount of nitrogen fertilizer. Irrigation practices such as alternate wetting and drying (AWD) have been shown to lower GHG emissions when compared to typical flooding methods. The time intervals between dry and wet circumstances aid in the shift from aerobic to anaerobic soil conditions, resulting in a considerable reduction in methane output. As a result, the project adopts the AWD approach to minimize CH 4 emissions. This will also result in a reduction in water use, lowering the farmer's input costs. Prior to the execution of the project activity, the farmers used the traditional flooding approach, which resulted in methane emissions into the atmosphere. The project proponent along with local implementation partner held training sessions and meetings with farmers to educate them on the benefits of using AWD, which was followed by the distribution and installation of AWD pipe in the fields of registered farmers. Location: The first instance of the project is located in Madhya Pradesh (Hoshangabad, Raisen, Sehore and Bhopal districts). The annual average emissions is 53,369 tCO 2 eq.

properties.project_name: Core Carbon Sustainable Rice Productions 04
properties.methodology: AMS-III.AU. Methane emission reduction by adjusted water management practice in rice cultivation
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Core Carbon Sustainable Rice Productions 04
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: Paddy fields are the most dominant anthropogenic sources of methane to the atmosphere (5-20% of the total emission from all anthropogenic sources ). Anaerobic decomposition of organic material in flooded rice fields produces methane, which escapes to the atmosphere primarily by transport through the rice plants. The annual amount of CH4 emitted from a given area of rice is a function of the number and duration of crops grown, water regimes before and during the cultivation period, and organic and inorganic soil amendments. Soil type, temperature, and rice cultivar also affect CH4 emissions. This CH4 emission-intensive cultivation method will be targeted by the proposed programme, that will involve the implementation of the technology/measures that result in reduced anaerobic decomposition of organic matter in rice cropping soils and thus reduced generation of methane. The project activity comprises of grouped projects of rice fields implementing the following methods: (a) Rice farms that change the water regime during the cultivation period from continuously to intermittent flooded conditions and/or a shortened period of flooded conditions; (b) Alternate wetting and drying method (AWD) (c) Rice farms that change their rice cultivation practice from transplanted to direct-seeded rice (DSR). Thus, the measure will consist of AWD and/or DSR in combination with adjusted water management system in rice cultivation. The Project Activity Instances will be implemented in Kamareddy district in the state of Telangana.  Each instance will be of 5000 Hectares will be implemented in Kamareddy, Telangana State.

properties.methodology: VMR0006 Energy Efficiency and Fuel Switch Measures in Thermal Applications

properties.verra_project_description: PROJECT SATHYA is an Improved Cookstoves and Livelihood project (hereafter referred to as “the Project” or “Project Sathya”) that aims for the sustainable development of the poor and marginalised communities residing in the core, buffer and fringe areas of the Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve, a protected area in Erode District, Tamil Nadu State, India (hereinafter referred to as “STR”).  Key activities of Project Sathya include: 1)	Installation and maintenance of 7500 Sarala brand improved cookstoves (“ICS”), which are fuel-efficient in-situ cookstoves with a chimney, that are constructed inside homes. This reduces fuelwood usage, air pollution, deforestation, human-animal conflict, health risks, poverty, and gender inequality. 2)	Creating awareness about the advantages of clean cooking practices and ongoing maintenance of devices to ensure continued health and economic benefits. 3)	Training of people from the community, primarily women, as cookstove makers to provide skilling, additional livelihood, supports higher adoption of devices and improves ongoing maintenance and usage. 4)	Training of community members in digital literacy, surveys, monitoring, project management, collaboration, and related skills to improve livelihood opportunities and reduce inequalities. 5)	Opening of bank accounts for members in the community to support financial inclusion and increase financial independence for women. 6)	Sourcing raw materials for cookstove making and installation from local micro, small and medium-sized enterprises to support economic development and employment opportunities in the region. 7)	Upgrading school infrastructure by supplying water filters, utensils, etc to support continued education and better health. 8)	Solar lighting in the villages to improve safety, reduce human-animal conflict and improve access to clean lighting. This Project supports SDGs 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15, and 17.

properties.project_name: CLEAN COOKSTOVE FOR GARO COMMUNITIES
properties.methodology: VMR0006 Energy Efficiency and Fuel Switch Measures in Thermal Applications
properties.verra_project_name_current: CLEAN COOKSTOVE FOR GARO COMMUNITIES
properties.verra_project_description: The proposed project aims at reducing the fuel wood consumption in traditional cook stoves by disseminating improved cook stoves (ICS) at a highly reduced cost of 200 INR. The transition from traditional to improved cookstoves will help in achieving significant firewood consumption that will enable climate change mitigation in a sustainable manner. Overall objective of the project is to improve the lives of the rural women by providing them with efficient cooking technology. This project will not only empower women, but also decrease fuelwood consumption at household level which will enable reduction of carbon emissions at a global scale. The project will ensure that just sources of renewable biomass are used that are in line with the requirements according to Glossary of CDM terms v 11.0. The existing scenario prior to the implementation of the project activity involves the usage of traditional mud cookstoves with poor ventilation, causing excessive indoor air pollution (IAP) and has been a serious health risk for women and children who spend several hours in the kitchen. The State of Meghalaya has an abundance of forest reserves and the ethnic communities rely on firewood for cooking. The state has three hill regions of the united Khasi and Jaintia Hills and Garo Hills. Garo Hills comprises of five district and the communities rely on traditional cooking practices and sources firewood from nearby forests. Penetration of modern cooking mediums like LPG gas, electric induction etc. have remained out of bound for most households in the region. The project activity is aimed to implement 20,000 cookstoves in the Meghalaya state of India. The Project activity had started distribution of Improved Cookstoves from 19th October 2022. The estimated annual emission reductions for this crediting period are 8,05,612 tCO2e and 1,15,087 tCO2e/year.

properties.project_name: Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL)
properties.methodology: VM0017 Adoption of Sustainable Agricultural Land Management
properties.project_type: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_primary_category: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_name_current: Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL)
properties.verra_sectoral_scope_current: Agriculture Forestry and Other Land Use
properties.verra_project_description: The Transformational Regenerative Integrated Biodiverse Agriculture for Livelihoods (TRIBAL) Project is a landscape approach that aims to make it viable for small and marginal farmers to live off their land in a sustainable and profitable manner. The project will promote agroforestry and sustainable farming practices across within the Araku Valley in Vishakhapatnam District, Andhra Pradesh, India. Planned agroforestry and sustainable farming practices that will be promoted by the project include agroforestry utilizing both fruit and multi-purpose tree species, shade coffee systems, intercropping of pulses and millets, green manuring, mulching and organic composting. These activities will improve the livelihoods and well-being of the tribal landowners by achieving multiple objectives such as improved soil fertility, increased revenue generation, food security, reduced drudgery for women and increased biodiversity. Through this positive impact on climate, communities, and biodiversity the TRIBAL project aims to achieve both VCS and CCB Gold certification. This grouped project is being initiated in Paderu and Pedabayalu Mandals of Paderu Division in Vishakhapatnam District, with the intention of expanding to up to 11 Mandals within the Araku Valley landscape in future. The tribal people of this region were traditionally hunters and gatherers, relying on the forest for sustenance. The practice of shifting cultivation came in at the turn of the century. As the- forest began to get depleted, the tribal communities gradually become engaged in agriculture. Now, subsistence agriculture is the primary livelihood for nearly 99% of the tribes within the project region, with over 80% of the landholdings being less than one hectare in size.

properties.project_name: Household Energy Efficiency Programme in East India

properties.verra_project_description: The purpose of this grouped project activity is to reduce       greenhouse gas emissions in the rural/semi urban households in India, by introducing energy efficient cookstoves, which will lead to a decrease in the use of non-renewable biomass (e.g., firewood). The ICS disseminated through this project will replace the baseline cookstoves. The first instance under this grouped project, will be implemented within the state boundary of the eastern states of India i.e., West Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, Jharkhand etc. It is envisaged that a combination of improved cook stoves (ICS) shall be provided to end user communities to completely replace baseline stoves. The ICS are designed to operate at higher efficiencies than the baseline stoves and result in reduced wood consumption as compared to baseline scenario. The overall effect is reduced emission of carbon dioxide and smoke, improving air quality within the household as well as the quality of life of women folk. At present the total stove distribution under this project activity is set at 3,500,000 out of which 3,000,000 will be Baldwin stoves and 500,000 Dinabandhu stoves for end user households. Each home will receive either a single Dinabandhu Cookstove or two Baldwin Cookstoves as part of the distribution of the stoves. However, the number of stoves that will be given to end user will depend on various factors such as household size, it’s cooking requirement etc. and the project proponent and/or the implementing partner shall have the discretion to decide on the combination as well as number of stoves each beneficiary household will receive. This is to ensure that the end user is not forced to go back to using baseline stoves on account of one project stove not being able to cater to complete requirements of the household.

properties.verra_project_description: This project will promote tree-based wild silk production (sericulture) outside traditional forests by utilizing privately owned degraded lands that smallholder farmers currently do not significantly utilize for productive purposes. It will undertake host tree planting for the Tasar silkworm and silkworm rearing value chain development in two states in India: Jharkhand and West Bengal. Traditionally, the tribal communities in these areas depend significantly on forests for their livelihoods and have a long history of silk production from natural forests –silk is second to agriculture as a source of income/livelihoods. However, production from the forests have become uncertain due to government regulation of forest access rights and instability in the silk market. Yet there are large areas in these regions that are severely degraded, fallow, etc. that would benefit from restoring their productive capacity and biodiversity through profitable tree planting investments. Therefore, this project will undertake tree planting for Tasar production on an estimated 3,000 ha of such lands. The project is implemented by the Non-Governmental Organization (NGO): PRADAN - Professional Assistance for Development Action – which has a long-standing experience (50 years) in the area. It will involve the participation of ~4,000 households in 117 villages, grouped into two clusters. The project has a crediting period of 20-years renewable, and will employ the new VERRA ARR Methodology ”Methodology for Afforestation, Reforestation, and Revegetation Projects”. Its estimated annual average and total GHG emission removals are 89,847 and 1,796,931 t CO2e respectively.

properties.verra_project_description: The Nagaland 4 Change is proposing an AFOLU Project under REDD+ Category in Peren district of Nagaland, North-eastern India. Nagaland is one of the few states of India having forest cover more than 50% of its geographical area. The forests provide multiple goods and services to the local Naga communities, such as fruits, seeds, medicines and recreation. Moreover, Nagaland state is located in the Indo-Burma Biodiversity Hotspot Region, which is among the 36 most biodiverse regions of the Earth. Some of the rare and endangered species, such as Spotted Linsang (Prionodon pardicolor), Clouded Leopard (Neofelis nebulosa), and Black Softshell Turtle (Nilssonia nigricans). In addition, forests of Nagaland protect the fragile hilly ecosystems of the state by preventing soil erosion and landslides.  However, specifically forests in Peren are gradually reducing in size. As well as the forests are also becoming increasingly prone to the fires during the dry summer months (April, May and June). Because of high anthropogenic pressures, the forests are also under extreme stress as a result of firewood collections. Therefore, Nagaland 4 Change, the Project Proponent is proposing a forest conservation project through funding from carbon financing under Verra VCS Mechanism. The main aim of the projects are as follows: 1.	Conservation of existing forests by protecting the forest cover. 2.	Increasing the forest cover as well as increasing density of the vegetation in forests. 3.	Enhancing the capacity of carbon storage of the forests, therefore generating carbon credits revenue out of it. 4.	Monitoring and reporting of the rare and endangered flora and fauna living the forests. 5.	Providing livelihood improvement to the local Naga communities through various interventions such as improved cookstoves, clean drinking water, etc.

The first instance of the grouped project will be implemented in Sagar Island and Namkhana of South 24 Paraganas, and it will concern 417 ha. This project is a one of a kind, with a holistic approach ensuring successful restoration and conservation of the largest mangrove forest in the world. This project will be generating GHG emissions reductions by conserving and restoring degraded mangroves, as well as generating removals by increasing the biomass by planting millions of mangrove trees in the project area. The project is planned for an initial duration of 20 years and 4.1 million tCO2e are estimated to be removed over the crediting period, corresponding to an average of 209k tCO2 per year. Regarding the first instance of the grouped project, approx. 654K tCO2e are estimated to be removed over 20 years. Sundari aims to lower the pressure on the mangrove due to a high dependency of the populations on the mangrove forests for fuelwood collection and fishing. The project seeks to reduce these threats by conducting capacity building with local communities and improving sustainable local livelihoods to ensure the permanence of the carbon as well as the ecosystem services provided. Sundari is entirely community-based and was designed in close relationship with the local communities. The project developer, Meensou India Private Limited, is a local limited company implanted in the region with extensive expertise in mangrove ecology and carbon projects. EcoAct will act as co-project owner of the Sundari project and will oversee/help with the project validation and verification as well as administrate KPIs.

properties.verra_project_description: Grow Indigo is implementing a project in Maharashtra and Gujarat to boost smallholder farmers' income through the adoption of regenerative agriculture, resulting in reduced greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and positive environmental and economic outcomes. The proposed project in Maharashtra and Gujarat addresses the GHG emissions caused by traditional agricultural practices in crops such as cotton, sugarcane, rice, wheat, maize, or soybean, without excluding other crops. Intensive agriculture practices in the project area have posed threats to land sustainability and contributed to increased GHG emissions. The project aims to promote regenerative agricultural practices, such as optimized fertilizer management, cover cropping, zero- or reduced-tillage, improved water management/ irrigation, crop rotation, and agroforestry, to restore soil health, enhance biodiversity, and improve productivity. The project takes an integrated and science-backed approach, including agricultural extension, outreach, agronomic support, digital data collection, and biogeochemical modeling. The project will initially target 40,000 hectares in the project area and cover diverse cropping systems with regenerative agricultural practices that are known to reduce GHG emissions (N2O, CO2e, and SOC) and thus generate carbon credits. The project also aims to link smallholder farmers to voluntary carbon markets, providing them with additional income opportunities and incentivizing the adoption of regenerative agriculture. With a cash incentive, smallholder farmers in the project boundary will adopt these practices more readily and contribute to sustainability and reduce GHG emissions. Through these efforts, the project seeks to contribute to sustainability, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and improve the overall livelihoods of smallholder farmers in the project area.

The entire project lies within the geographical boundaries of Telangana state in India. In the first instance, the project activity is limited to the district of Nalgonda. Being a grouped project, more farmers and communities belonging to other districts of Telangana will be added as ‘future project instances. The project activity involves planting oil palm trees along with some cash crops like turmeric and groundnuts. In the first project instance, around 1,100 Ha will be covered in Nalgonda district in three years.  Future instances will cover 15 other districts of the state of Telangana. All project instances within this grouped project activity will consist of afforestation, reforestation and revegetation (ARR) primarily involving oil palm plantations with intercropping of turmeric and groundnuts. Tapovanam is the coordinator for all the participating farmers and provides training to the farmers regarding the technologies/measures involved in the project activity. Tapovanam will have the right to carbon credits without any violation of farmers rights. The revenue after expenses from sale of carbon credits will be shared with the participating farmers. Clime Trek is the Carbon Project Developer.
